check.name: lens.design
check.reason: Melian shares none of this text, which the reviewing host's store and terminal hold

message.text: The change makes exit 125 inconclusive inside `probeConclusive`. That function is also the second half of `runStands`, through `probesConclusive`, so any finished probing run that holds one 125 probe can no longer be reused. The change does not limit this to reruns. Exit 125 is deterministic: the probe uses it to say it cannot test its attack. The tests lens's own wording tells the prober to exit 125 whenever the named test already fails on the unchanged copy, and `run_probe` now offers 125 to every lens. Running such a run again gets the same 125, so a run that read `ran` and clean is planned and probed again on every repeat review of an unchanged head.

evidence.snippet: Status: the maintainer ruled on 2026-11-16, in the coordinator's session, as [issue #514](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/issues/514) records: "Whether probing or not, a lens with the same running parameters (including the fact that it is a probing lens) on the same code, should not be run again." He asked for the change to be fast-tracked, said he accepts the risk, and said the installed dependencies of the code under test need not be in the key. The issue asked for this file to supersede [the 2026-11-14 decision](2026-11-14-probing-runs-not-reused.md). The builder amends it instead: two active decisions amend it, and the decision index refuses an amendment of a superseded decision, so superseding it would mean superseding both of them and the decision that amends one of those.

That costs each repeat a probing run, $0.65 to $1.69 and about four minutes on the first four host rounds. Probing is not deterministic, so a repeat can also report a finding its first run did not. Example: a finisher records a dismissal and repeats the round to publish the verdict. The probing lens runs again and may block a pull request that had just read clean.

2. **Every probe it tried ended conclusively.** `probesConclusive` in `packages/pipeline/src/probing.ts` reads the prober's `ProbingDocument`: each `run_probe` call's ID in `attempts` must have a stored result, and that result must be conclusive by `probeConclusive`, the definition the rerun task uses. A probe the sandbox refused leaves an attempt with no result; one that timed out, was cut or was ended by a signal says nothing. A run holding one is not reused, and the next review of that head plans and probes again.

Three reviews found the three cases this rule closes, each a place where reuse asked a narrower question than the record. Codex's adversarial review at `b4dd5bef` found a prober that failed over to a fallback the committed tier refuses: the record failed the lens, but the copy and `--rerun` read only the planner's model. The Actions round at `b4dd5bef` found a run whose prober left an attack unanswered: the record read ended, but reuse read only the top-level `done`. The review of record at `b4dd5bef` found a run whose every probe the sandbox refused: the prober reported nothing, so the record read ran and clean, and every later review of that head copied it and never probed again. In each, the review stayed wrong until its request changed.

A prober on a tier of its own is not judged by model, since its check's lineage does not yet hold it, as [the prober-tier limit](2026-11-14-prober-tier-lineage-limit.md) says; judging it by the level's policy would refuse a model its own tier accepts. A probing outcome names no other model: a failover leaves only the model each conversation finished on, and a run a quick one escalates to is an outcome of its own.

What the second half costs: a head whose probes keep timing out, on a loaded machine say, or that the sandbox keeps refusing, is planned and probed again on every review until its probes end conclusively. Each such review pays for the probing run again, $0.65 to $1.69 and about four minutes on the first four host rounds.

- A stored rerun that failed or passed stands for every repeat review of its head. One that timed out, was cut or ended by a signal runs again on a repeat review, as a refused one does, since its cause may have passed.

probes: `${probeIs} To change the code, copy the checkout into a folder under TMPDIR and work in the copy, leaving out node_modules and anything that is neither a file, a folder nor a link, such as the device the sandbox puts where a file such as .npmrc might hold a credential. Give the copy a node_modules directory of its own holding a link to each top-level entry of the checkout's, since a test runner writes beside its dependencies, and point any link to one of the repository's own packages at that package in the copy. Run the test file the attack names on the unchanged copy first, then change the behaviour the attack names, one line where one line will do, and run it again. Run the test runner through node, as node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs --run <file> runs Vitest, since npx is not on PATH. Exit 1 when the test passes with the behaviour changed, the attack's failing outcome, since no test fails for it; exit 0 when it fails, its passing outcome. When the test already fails on the unchanged copy, the probe cannot show whether the test covers the behaviour: print what it printed, exit 125, and report no finding. Print the line you changed and what the test printed each time, since the output is the evidence. A probe that only restates the claim, or fails for a reason of its own such as a syntax error, shows nothing.`,

"Run a probe for one attack of the plan: a Node ES module, run as probe.mjs with your files beside it, in a read-only checkout of the head with no network. Exit 0 for the attack's passing outcome, 125 when the probe cannot test its attack, and any other non-zero code when it shows the defect. Returns the probe's ID, its exit, and its output.",

explanation.whatToDo: Keep 125 out of the attack-answered and failed-again checks, but let a run whose 125 probes the prober answered with a skip still stand for reuse. For example, give `probesConclusive` its own check that treats exit 125 as settled. Or amend the reuse decision on purpose and record that a run holding a 125 probe is asked again on every review.
explanation.whyHere: The active base decision on reusing finished probing runs carries the maintainer's ruling that a lens with the same running parameters on the same code "should not be run again". It keeps out of reuse only probes that say nothing because their cause may pass, such as a timeout under load or a refused sandbox, and its cost section names only those. This change lifts the tests lens's probing refusal, so the deterministic 125 case is now reachable in real rounds. The head decisions amend only the probe-reruns decision, which covers the rerun of a cited probe, not reuse of the whole lens run. No head decision amends the reuse decision.

properties.failureScenario: A repository's `tests-probes` lens extends `tests` and probes at `deep`, which `Lens.load` now allows. For a head whose named test already fails on main, the tests prober follows its wording: it runs the test on the unchanged copy, prints the output and exits 125. `describeProbe` says the probe shows nothing, the reminder asks for a skip, and the prober skips the attack with a reason. The lens records `ran` and clean. The finisher records a dismissal and repeats the round to publish. On that repeat, `runStands` (review.ts:1450) calls `probesConclusive`, which calls `probeConclusive`. That returns false for `exitCode: 125`, so the finished task is replaced. The tests probing lens is planned and probed again, at $0.65 to $1.69 and about four minutes per review by the reuse decision's own figures. It does this on every later repeat of the same head, forever, because the test keeps failing and the probe keeps exiting 125. Because probing is not deterministic, any one of those repeats can report a finding the first run did not, and block a pull request that had just read clean. That is the outcome the reuse decision was made to stop. The same happens to a trust-boundary or correctness run whose prober used the 125 that `run_probe` now advertises.
